The dynamic endpoints this workspace publishes. A dynamic endpoint is a URL that starts a workflow: another system sends a request to it, the request body becomes the workflow's payload, and the workflow decides what comes back. That is often simpler than the API when a system only needs to push data in.

Each entry says where to send the request, whether it needs a token, which origins a browser may call it from, and what it answers with, so an integration can be wired up from this listing alone. The JWT key and secret are never returned.

Only endpoints on a published workflow are listed, because those are the only ones that answer a request. Reading this list needs the same permission as viewing workflows. Endpoints are created on the workflow, so this is a listing and nothing else.

403.description: The role this key belongs to may not view workflows.

name.description: The name given to the endpoint on the workflow.

url.description: The address to send the request to. Treat it as a secret: whoever holds it can run the workflow.

authentication_required.description: Whether a request has to carry a signed JWT, in an `Authorization: Bearer` header or a `token` header. When false, holding the URL is all it takes.

cors_origins.description: The origins a browser may call this endpoint from. Null means cross-origin calls are off, so only server-to-server calls get through. A single `*` means any origin.

response_type.description: What the endpoint sends back. `data` and `html` return a fixed body, `redirect` sends a 302, `continue` lets the workflow decide, and `sse` streams events as the workflow runs.
